awd_titl_txt: I-Corps: Translation Potential of an Extensible Approach for Microbial Profiling from Sequencing Data
awd_abstract_narration:
The significance of this I-Corps project is based on the translation from lab to market of an artificial intelligence (AI)-powered microbial profiling platform that analyzes DNA sequencing data with enhanced speed, accuracy, and scalability. The benefits of this approach include increased scalability, reduced processing time, and improved sensitivity for detecting rare microbial species. Microbial profiling is crucial for applications in public health, infectious disease and environmental monitoring, precision medicine, and pharmaceutical development. For example, in the U.S. alone, healthcare-associated infections affect over 1.7 million patients annually and current sequence analysis workflows are too resource-intensive to scale effectively, creating a significant barrier to timely and cost-efficient microbial detection. By reducing the computational burden and expertise required for sequencing analysis, this innovation may expand access to genomic insights, facilitating advances in healthcare, biotechnology, and biosecurity while reducing costs for clinical and research institutions.

This I-Corps project utilizes experiential learning coupled with a first-hand investigation of the industry ecosystem to assess the translation potential of a microbial profiling platform powered by large language models (LLMs). This approach processes DNA sequencing data as a structured language, applying deep learning techniques to recognize taxonomic patterns, host-microbe interactions, plasmid differentiation, and antibiotic resistance markers. This new solution consists of a two-step artificial intelligence (AI) framework: (1) foundational LLMs pre-trained on extensive sequencing datasets to learn genomic patterns and (2) a fine-tuning mechanism that customizes model predictions for domain-specific microbial profiling. Unlike conventional alignment-based sequencing analysis which requires extensive computational resources and bioinformatics expertise, this method rapidly extracts meaningful biological insights with minimal manual intervention and further automates data interpretation, optimizing results for clinical and research applications. The ability to rapidly analyze microbial communities with high accuracy has significant implications for infectious disease management, antimicrobial resistance tracking, and precision medicine applications.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
The NSF I-Corps project, Translation Potential of an Extensible Approach for Microbial Profiling from Sequencing Data, explored the commercialization potential of advanced artificial intelligence (AI) technologies for analyzing DNA sequencing and other omics data. Our company is developing Genomics AI solutions that treat DNA as a language and apply large language model (LLM) techniques to rapidly interpret genomics data. These technologies have applications across healthcare, infectious disease surveillance, agriculture, biotechnology, environmental monitoring, and basic scientific research.

The intellectual merit of this project lies in advancing the emerging field of Genomics AI. Our technology aims to improve how researchers and practitioners analyze complex biological data by reducing computational requirements while increasing accuracy, scalability, and access to biological knowledge. Through the I-Corps program, we evaluated how these innovations could address real-world challenges in microbial profiling, pathogen detection, antibiotic resistance monitoring, and other genomics applications. We also identified customer segments that would benefit most from these technologies and assessed their willingness to adopt and pay for such solutions.

As part of the NSF I-Corps curriculum, our team completed extensive customer discovery training and conducted more than 200 interviews with stakeholders across academia, healthcare, biotechnology, pharmaceutical companies, government organizations, and industry. Interviewees included CEOs, directors, bioinformaticians, biostatisticians, researchers, clinicians, and technology leaders. These conversations helped us better understand customer needs, refine our value proposition, identify priority market segments, and guide future technology development.

The broader impacts of this project extend beyond scientific advancement. Insights gained through customer discovery accelerated the commercialization pathway for Genomics AI technologies that can improve public health decision-making, strengthen infectious disease surveillance, enable more efficient biomedical research, and enhance agricultural and environmental monitoring. The project also contributed to workforce development by strengthening entrepreneurial skills within the research team and fostering collaboration between academia and industry.

As a direct outcome of this award, we secured matching support from our university, advanced multiple Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) proposals, expanded partnerships with potential customers and collaborators, and were accepted into Cohort 3 of the Paratus Digital Health Accelerator supported by BARDA. These accomplishments demonstrate growing market demand for AI-powered genomics technologies and have accelerated the development of our minimum viable product (MVP), positioning the company for continued innovation, commercialization, job creation, and economic growth in the rapidly expanding biotechnology and artificial intelligence sectors.
